title: Adaptive Escalation Simulator and Playbook Compatibility Checker
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds an offline escalation simulator and automated playbook compatibility checks. No user-facing behavior changes.
description:
Motivation:
This PR introduces an offline escalation simulator and a playbook compatibility checker designed to catch gaps between runbook steps and real telemetry formats before incidents hit oncall. Multiple recent handoffs revealed brittle steps that assume specific event shapes or exact labels; the simulator lets engineers run synthetic incident flows against a target playbook and flags mismatches, missing verification steps, and timing assumptions that can cause flaky human responses.

What this changes (high level):
- New CLI: `ib-sim run` to execute a configurable escalation scenario against a playbook, with optional recorded-telemetry input or generated synthetic traces.
- Playbook compatibility checker: static + dynamic checks that validate required signals, required alert annotations, and handoff artifacts (attachments, runbook links).
- A small shim to normalize historical telemetry snapshots into the simulator input format to make regression checks reproducible.
- Templates and example scenarios under `/examples/esc-scenarios/` for common SLO breach, noise, and flapping conditions.
- Unit and integration tests; CI pipeline step that runs a smoke scenario on PRs labeled `incident-bot` to prevent regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] RFC reviewed by SRE and oncall leads (ENG-4921)
- [x] Tests covering static analysis and two scenario end-to-end flows
- [x] Docs: quickstart and example scenarios added to `doc/ops-sim.md`
- [x] Metrics for simulator runs (duration, mismatch_count) instrumented

Commits (summary):
- feat(sim): add core simulator runner and scenario DSL (4 commits)
- feat(checker): playbook compatibility static analyzer, rule set, test harness
- feat(cli): ib-sim entrypoint + config parsing + output formatters
- fix(tests): deterministic fixtures for telemetry normalization
- docs: ops-sim quickstart and example scenarios

Files/areas touched (high level):
- cmd/ib-sim/main.go (new CLI)
- internal/sim/runner.go, sim/scenario_dsl.go, sim/normalizer.go
- internal/checker/compatibility.go, checker/rules/*.go
- examples/esc-scenarios/*.yaml
- doc/ops-sim.md
- ci/workflows/sim-smoke.yml (new CI job)
- tests/integration/sim_endtoend_test.go

How it works (short):
- The simulator consumes a scenario (sequence of alert events + timing hints) and a playbook ID. It first runs static checks (does the playbook reference signals that exist, required annotations present?), then executes the scenario against the playbook runner, mapping actions to expected signals and verifying handoff artifacts. The compatibility checker returns categorized findings: missing-signal, ambiguous-step, brittle-timing, and attachment-mismatch. Findings include suggested fixes where possible (e.g., add signal mapping, add an explicit verification step).

Review notes & decisions made during review:
- Marcus: asked for a sampling mode for long scenarios; implemented via `--sample-rate` and added a short-circuit in the runner for CI smoke runs.
- Yvonne: requested clearer severity levels for findings; added `severity` field and mapping table in compatibility.go and updated docs.
- Diego: asked to avoid expanding runtime dependencies; replaced a third-party YAML parser with standard library helpers and small stable helper code.
- Author replies: noted tradeoffs and added comments linking to ENG-5032 for follow-up UX work to visualize findings in the Console.

CI summary:
- New `sim-smoke` job runs on PR label `incident-bot` and executes two small scenarios; all checks passed in the final run. Unit tests: 142 passed, 0 failed. Integration smoke: passed. Lint: passed. Flaky tests: one network-tied test was quarantined (see test tag) and will be addressed in a follow-up.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash by Yvonne Chen on 2026-03-05 after approval from Marcus and Diego. Commit message kept as the summarized feature list and pointers to ENG-4921 and ENG-5032.

Follow-ups planned (tracked):
- ENG-5032: Console visualization for findings and per-playbook historical trend charts.
- ENG-5410: Expand scenario library with customer-derived incident traces (privacy review required).
- Small follow-up to move long-running scenarios to a scheduled job and provide a web UI for running simulations on demand.

Notes for maintainers:
- Exported metrics use `sim.` prefix; add retention in observability-pack if you want longer retention.
- The compatibility rule set is intentionally conservative; if you want a permissive mode use `--permissive` which lowers severity on missing optional signals.
